## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ānisaṁsadassāvīkathā* ("Debate on One Who Sees the Advantage") is the first discourse in the ninth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, belonging to the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The debate addresses the thesis that for one who contemplates or perceives the advantage (*ānisaṁsadassāvī*), there is abandoning (*pahāna*) of mental fetters [Bareau 1955]. This view, attributed to the Andhaka school, appeals to sutta teachings—specifically connected with the *Nibbānasutta* (AN 7.19)—concerning one who abides observing happiness in Extinction [SuttaCentral; Bareau 1955]. The orthodox Theravādin position rejects this assertion, contending that abandoning does not occur merely through discerning advantages; rather, defilements are abandoned only by applying attention to the impermanence (*anicca*), suffering (*dukkha*), disease, vanity, and nonself (*anatta*) of conditioned formations (*saṅkhārā*) [Bareau 1955].

No cross-language matches in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan are identified for this text [DharmaNexus]. Computational analysis reveals extensive Pali-internal text reuse across 21 texts with 131 matching passages [DharmaNexus]. Significant internal parallels occur elsewhere in the *Kathāvatthu*, particularly with the *Adhigayhamanasikārakathā* (Kv 16.4, sharing over 1,700 characters in §3.1–3.15), the *Nirodhakathā* (Kv 10.1), the *Ariyantikathā* (Kv 3.2), and the *Sabbasaṁyojanappahānakathā* (Kv 4.10) [DharmaNexus]. Formulaic and thematic parallels also link segment §2.4–2.25 with the *Visuddhimagga*, the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 2), the *Cullaniddesa* (Cnd 5, Cnd 11), the *Milindapañha* (Mil 7.8.7), and the text's commentary in the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
